authority: Parliament of India / Ministry of Law and Justice

sources.title: What Agreements are Contracts
sources.summary: All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void.

sources.title: What Considerations and Objects are Lawful
sources.summary: The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless it is forbidden by law, or is of such nature that, if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law, or is fraudulent, or involves injury to person or property, or is regarded as immoral or opposed to public policy.

sources.title: Agreement in Restraint of Trade Void
sources.summary: Every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void, subject to standard exceptions regarding the sale of goodwill.

sources.title: Agreements in Restraint of Legal Proceedings Void
sources.summary: Every agreement by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract by the usual legal proceedings in ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may enforce his rights, is void to that extent.

sources.title: Compensation for Loss or Damage Caused by Breach / Penalty Clauses
sources.summary: Section 73 provides compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract that naturally arose in the usual course of things. Section 74 stipulates that when a contract contains a penalty or liquidated damages clause, the court awards only reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount named, regardless of actual loss proved.
